summary.text: Sam Liccardo is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 16th Congressional District, which runs from Half Moon Bay and Pacifica through Silicon Valley, including San Jose, Palo Alto and Mountain View. A former prosecutor, San Jose City Council member and two-term mayor of San Jose, he was first elected to Congress in 2024 and sits on the House Financial Services Committee. His campaign materials emphasize housing, lowering the cost of living, and bipartisan legislation.

paragraphs.text: Liccardo was born on April 16, 1970. According to his Ballotpedia survey he grew up in the district he now represents, and Ballotpedia lists Bellarmine College Preparatory as his high school.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Georgetown University in 1991, and a law degree and a master's degree in public policy from Harvard's Kennedy School, both in 1996.

Liccardo worked as a prosecutor of sexual assault and child exploitation crimes in the Santa Clara County District Attorney's Office and as a federal prosecutor in the Southern District of California; in his Ballotpedia survey he also lists college professor among his past roles.

He was elected to the San Jose City Council (District 3) in 2006, served from 2007 to 2015 and won re-election in 2010. He was elected mayor of San Jose in November 2014 and re-elected in 2018, serving two terms through 2022.
His House website says San Jose committed to carbon neutrality, expanded community-based policing and launched its largest rent relief program during his tenure.
Liccardo won the open U.S. House seat in November 2024, defeating fellow Democrat Evan Low to succeed Anna Eshoo, and took office in 2025.

He serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and chairs the New Democratic Coalition's Innovation & Technology Working Group; his House website says he led the New Dems' first Innovation Agenda in July 2025.
According to his House website, he and his wife, Jessica Garcia-Kohl, a nonprofit leader, live in Saratoga.
